upstream.note: The newest stable cmark release. Its own pinned spec.txt is the CommonMark corpus, so the reference implementation and language version move atomically.

claim: For CommonMark syntax, Markdown Core tracks the newest stable cmark reference release. cmark-gfm has no authority in this scope. Deliberate AST-model differences and reviewed upstream defects are the only registered deltas.

deltas.summary: An HTML comment is a `Comment` node whose literal is the bytes between `<!--` and `-->`: the inline token, and an HTML block that opens with `<!--` and whose end line holds only whitespace after the first `-->`. Upstream keeps both as html nodes holding the token as written.
deltas.handling: The shared normalizer maps upstream's comment nodes to `Comment` with the delimiters removed, which is the rule the engine applies on its own side (`docs/specs/dialect/comments.md`), and records that the projection acted. A model difference, so a projection rather than a list of inputs; the token and block boundaries are upstream's and are compared unchanged.

deltas.summary: cmark keeps a scanned title in its reference map after the definition parser rewinds it into paragraph text. Markdown Core drops the title so the map agrees with the accepted definition.
deltas.rationale: The pinned CommonMark specification says the example is a link reference definition with no title, and remark/micromark independently resolves it without one.
deltas.handling: Keyed to the exact specification regression input; erasing all titles would hide real title-resolution defects.

deltas.summary: The dialect's text directive claims a colon-led name, `:abc`, wherever the directives module admits one; CommonMark leaves the bytes as text.
deltas.rationale: The dialect index lists directives as a feature of the one language, judged by remark (`pnpm check:mdast-parity`), and remark-directive parses the same input to the same text directive.
deltas.handling: Keyed to the exact specification input.

deltas.summary: cmark can emit a Text node with an empty literal after hard-break processing. Markdown Core and mdast omit nodes that own no content.
deltas.handling: The shared normalizer drops empty Text nodes on both sides and records that the projection acted.

corpus.note: The corpus comes from the same immutable cmark commit as the reference binary.
Only regressions with no extension tag belong to the CommonMark language.

The inputs of cmark's smart_punct.txt, compared without `--smart` on either side: the dialect has no smart punctuation, so quotation marks, hyphen runs, and periods are stored as written and the two parsers agree byte for byte.
The comments module's HTML-comment examples: cmark owns the token and block boundaries, and the `html-comment-node` projection states the one model difference.

The links-and-images module's destination examples: cmark owns the link and image grammar, and its `Destination` is the `url` branch of the dialect's tagged value. The module's GFM autolink section is cmark-gfm's to judge.

corpusNote: cmark is the sole primary implementation oracle for CommonMark syntax and its own pinned 0.31.2 spec is compared in full. Both sides parse every input as their whole language: the dialect has no switches, so this gate judges what ships, and every place the dialect deliberately leaves CommonMark is registered above as a projection or keyed to its exact inputs. The product's extension fixtures are not in this corpus; their syntax is judged by cmark-gfm, remark, and the product fixtures themselves.
